sections.overview: The catalogue name Pristis perotteti is now treated as a synonym of Pristis pristis, the largetooth sawfish; this entry therefore describes that currently recognized species rather than a separate taxon.
sections.identification: This is a ray, not a shark: its flattened head and long, toothed rostrum give sawfishes their distinctive outline.
sections.habitat: It occurs in tropical river systems and estuaries. Adults also use coastal waters.
sections.diet: It feeds on fishes and bottom-dwelling invertebrates, using its saw to disturb sediment or strike at prey.
sections.behavior: The long rostrum is a hunting tool as well as a conspicuous identifying feature.
sections.reproduction: Its life history is poorly known; Australian accounts describe slow maturation and low reproductive output.
sections.ecology: Its use of rivers, estuaries and coastal waters links freshwater and marine ecosystems.
sections.conservation: The global assessment of Pristis pristis is Critically Endangered; entanglement in fishing gear and loss or alteration of habitat are major concerns.
